exposure: Gestational age at delivery (22-24 weeks and 25-27 weeks)
cohort: Women who delivered at 22-27 weeks of gestation (n=647) at two level III units in Sweden
finding: Cesarean section performed at 22-27 weeks of gestation was not associated with increased short-term maternal morbidity compared to cesarean section at term, but was associated with more major complications.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery at 22-24 weeks of gestation was associated with a higher rate of incisions other than low transverse compared to 25-27 weeks.
